title: MeitY Advisory to Social Media Intermediaries on Manipulated and Synthetic Content (8 October 2026)
summary: On 8 October 2026 MeitY's Cyber Laws Division issued an advisory (File No. 16(2)/2026-CyberLaws) to all social media intermediaries. It asks them to exercise enhanced diligence over false, manipulated or out-of-context content that could affect public order; to identify and label or contextualise manipulated, synthetic or misleading content, especially content presented as a current event; and to prioritise complaints from authorised government agencies. Unlike the February 2026 IT Rules amendment, its labelling request is not limited to audio-visual content. It refers to duties under the IT Act and IT Rules, takes immediate effect, and states no specific penalties.
key_obligations: Label or contextualise manipulated, synthetic or misleading content
Prioritise complaints from authorised government agencies on public-order content
Run user awareness measures on verifying information before sharing
Strengthen monitoring, escalation and grievance-redressal systems

sources.title: MeitY widens labelling for social media beyond synthetic content
Amid SIR stir, MeitY asks social media platforms to prioritise govt complaints, label 'misleading' content
